messages.author: dc8b4131b39a099f
messages.subject: Suggestions for validating models
parts:
Dear unmarked users-

We have fit and selected n-mixture models with habitat covariates at
the plot- and landscape-level for 23 forest passerine species, based
on data from four watersheds. I now have the luxury (for the first
time!) of an independent data set from a fifth watershed within the
same ecosystem for use in validating our models, but I'm not sure how
to go about it. I was thinking of using our models and associated
coefficient/beta values for habitat covariates (based on the original
data) to predict spp relative abundance with the values of the habitat
covariates in the validation watershed, and then regressing/
correlating the new predictions with the observed values of spp
relative abundance from the validation watershed. However, assuming
this is a valid approach, I'm not sure how to handle the detection
error associated with the observed relative abundance data from the
validation watershed. Perhaps we should "manually" correct the
observed abundance data with the predicted estimates of detection
error from the original models, before regressing the new predictions
with the observed values? Or maybe you are aware of different
methods? Most of the literature I have found is focused on using
"resampling" methods (ROC curves, jackknife, cross-validation,
bootstrapping, etc.) to assess model fit without the availability of
an independent data set for validation.

Thanks in advance for your input. Best regards,

Matt

parts:
hi Matt,
 You have data in the form of counts y[i,j] from this new watershed?  It seems to me that you can use the existing model to produce predictions of these new observations, yhat[i,j], say, and then just compare y[i,j] with yhat[i,j].
 There is no need that the evaluation has to be in terms of the underlying state-variable. In fact, as you've noted, that is not straightforward.
 If I'm misunderstanding something please re-ask.
regards,
andy

messages.author: 527e14923215b7e4
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Suggestions for validating models
parts:
Hi Matt,

I believe what Andy is suggesting is that you compare the observed counts in your "test" watershed (y.test) with the model's predictions (y.hat). Something like this should work:

lam.hat <- predict(yourmodel, newdata=testdata, type="state")[,1]
lam.hat <- matrix(lam.hat, M, J)
p.hat <- predict(yourmodel, newdata=testdata, type="det")[,1]
p.hat <- matrix(p.hat, M, J)

y.hat <- lam.hat * p.hat

So now you just need a measure of predictive error to compare y.hat with y.test (your counts from the new watershed). Something like this might suffice, but you should consult a good text

pred.error <- mean(abs(y.test - y.hat))

You could use this to rank candidate models by their predictive performance (at least the ability to predict data in your new watershed)

Best,
Richard
